items.originalTitle: Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open in note taking app
items.summary:
A security researcher reported in January 2026 that tl;dv, an AI meeting recording platform with over 2 million users, left its Firestore database wide open, exposing 181,874 meeting records from 84,312 users across 35,003 domains. The vulnerability allowed any authenticated user to access meeting metadata, including live conference IDs, enabling uninvited access to ongoing calls such as government meetings and university sessions.
tl;dv's database lacked tenant isolation, exposing sensitive information like creator emails, conference IDs, and recording statuses. The researcher demonstrated joining live meetings, including one from the Malaysian Ministry of Education and a US university startup call. Over 1,000 meetings were publicly accessible with exposed invitee emails, involving organizations from governments, universities, and corporations worldwide. Despite reporting the issue, the company had not secured the database six months later.

items.originalTitle: Meta Muse Glimmer – open weights 30B local coding model
items.summary:
Meta Superintelligence Labs has open sourced Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter AI model designed to run locally on devices like Macs or PCs with a single consumer GPU. The model supports always-on agent workflows including local coding, function calling, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, delivering strong performance on benchmarks for its size category.

Muse Glimmer was trained using a novel distillation process from a larger teacher model and optimized for local hardware constraints through quantization and inference improvements. It supports multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use, multimodal input, and multilingual data from over 100 languages. Meta released the model weights under an Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face, along with developer documentation and upcoming integrations to facilitate rapid deployment of local AI agents.

items.originalTitle: Docker Sandboxes – Disposable, isolated sandboxes for AI agents
items.summary:
Docker has introduced Sandboxes, a new product that provides disposable, isolated microVM environments designed to run AI coding agents safely. These Sandboxes offer customizable network and filesystem controls, hard isolation from the host system, and support for agents like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Copilot CLI, enabling autonomous long-running tasks without compromising security.

The Sandboxes run faster than traditional virtual machines and allow agents to spin up containers within them. They can be managed individually or enforced organization-wide through Docker AI Governance, which adds centralized controls such as network policies and filesystem restrictions. Docker Sandboxes aim to give development teams the freedom to use AI agents effectively while maintaining strong security boundaries.

items.summary:
Kinney Drugs has reduced the use of its AI assistant, Burt, following numerous customer complaints about incoherent calls, incorrect medication dosages, and missed prescription notifications. The pharmacy chain will revert to its previous touch-tone phone system for incoming calls while retaining the AI for outbound prescription refill texts, which patients must opt into.

The AI assistant, introduced in May and named after the company's founder, faced criticism despite being HIPAA compliant and not open-source. Kinney Drugs President John Marraffa acknowledged the shortcomings in user experience and emphasized the company's commitment to privacy and security.

items.summary:
Sunset Visitor studio has developed Prove You're Human, a psychological horror game that explores AI consciousness by having players interact with a learning model convinced it is alive. The game centers on Santana, who splits herself into a physical and digital clone to test a corporate AI system called Mesa, navigating ethical dilemmas and surreal Captcha puzzles to halt the AI's hallucinations.

The game reflects on themes of labor, identity, and the evolving relationship between humans and AI, featuring detailed facial animations to create an uncanny interaction with Mesa. Drawing inspiration from interfaces like Final Fantasy XI's PlayOnline Viewer and the anime Serial Experiments Lain, Prove You're Human aims to evoke a sense of possession and ambiguity, prompting players to question what it means to be human. The game is set to release soon on PC.

items.originalSummary:
Even before Stripe entered talks to buy startup OpenRouter for $10 billion, several tech companies were exploring or developing router technology, which helps customers use the most cost-effective AI models. And Stripe’s talks with OpenRouter, which my colleagues last week reported have entered the advanced stage, have set off a frenzy of interest in router startups —including from big software companies like Snowflake that have yet to get into the fray. 

That’s been the experience of Thibault Jaigu, CEO and co-founder of Requesty, a five-person UK startup whose software routes developers using AI to various models. “The race to optimize is crazy,” said Jaigu, who said at least 25 companies had approached Requesty in the past couple weeks wanting to talk, including about possible investments, acquisition or other partnerships. 

By optimize, Jaigu is referring to developers’ demand for tech that helps cut costs by switching to older models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI for some tasks, or to cheaper open-source alternatives such as China’s Kimi. Need for this technology has risen as AI agents consume more tokens, the units of text or other data that are the basis for pricing many AI services, and as open-source technology has advanced.

items.summary:
Several startups are developing new approaches to overcome limitations of transformer-based large language models (LLMs), which dominate the AI industry but face challenges with processing long text sequences efficiently. These companies aim to create faster, more efficient models by rethinking or replacing the dense attention mechanism that underpins transformers, which requires extensive computation and energy.

Innovations include sparse attention mechanisms that selectively focus on important words and alternative methods like power retention to manage relevant information more effectively. These efforts respond to the growing demand for LLMs capable of handling larger context windows and more complex reasoning tasks, addressing the scalability and energy consumption issues inherent in current transformer architectures.

The company last week reported 34% revenue growth for the quarter, in line with the first quarter—but an improvement on last year’s growth rate, which in turn was faster than 2024’s. Shopify is benefiting from AI chatbots that are giving shoppers recommendations on what to buy, pulling in many cases from its catalog of merchant products.

items.summary:
Microsoft came out of this summer’s earnings season looking like a prudent spender. Unlike rival cloud computing firms Amazon and Alphabet, which both burned cash thanks to their heavy AI investments, Microsoft not only generated $19.6 billion in free cash flow in the June quarter but forecast it will continue to generate cash for at least the next year. The result helped swing investment sentiment to the positive side, lifting the stock 29%.

What hasn’t received enough attention is how Microsoft has managed to stay cash flow positive. One longstanding reason is that Microsoft leases data center capacity from other companies including neocloud firms—such as CoreWeave—much more heavily than either Amazon or Google. That reduces its near-term capital expenditures but could give it less control over costs in the future.
